20 A wire is being stretched by a tensile force.
Which statement about the elastic limit must be correct?
A
The deformation is plastic after the elastic limit has been reached.
B
The deformation is plastic until the elastic limit is reached.
C
The extension is proportional to the tensile force after the elastic limit has been reached.
D
The extension is proportional to the tensile force until the elastic limit is reached.

hints: Notice the question says elastic limit, not limit of proportionality - recall where each point lies on a force-extension graph for a wire.
Connect proportionality with Hooke's law $F = kx$ and elastic behaviour with returning to original length - they stop at different points.
Ask what must happen on unloading once the elastic limit is exceeded compared with unloading before it is reached.
walkthrough: Identify the two different limits: the limit of proportionality is where extension stops being proportional to tensile force, while the elastic limit is where the material stops returning to its original length.
Recall that for many metals the force-extension graph stays elastic but curves after the limit of proportionality, so proportionality can be lost while behaviour is still elastic.
Therefore a statement that extension is proportional to force until the elastic limit is not always true, which rules out the proportionality statements.
By definition, loading beyond the elastic limit leaves a permanent extension after the tensile force is removed, which is plastic deformation.
This permanent set after the elastic limit has been reached is the only statement that must hold. This is option A.

A.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit the wire does not return to its original length when unloaded, so further deformation is plastic with permanent extension.

B.explanation: Below the elastic limit the wire returns to its original length on unloading, so the deformation is elastic not plastic.

C.explanation: Proportionality $F$ proportional to $x$ is lost at the limit of proportionality, so it cannot hold after the elastic limit is passed.

D.explanation: Proportionality stops at the limit of proportionality, which can occur before the elastic limit, so it is not guaranteed up to the elastic limit.
